data.title: Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG)
data.summary: Biologicals · Pooled polyclonal IgG from thousands of healthy donors
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Biologicals_

**Class:** Pooled polyclonal IgG from thousands of healthy donors

## Mechanism of action
- Saturates the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) → faster breakdown of pathogenic autoantibodies (key in pemphigus)
- Blocks Fas–FasL interaction → stops keratinocyte apoptosis (proposed in TEN)
- Neutralises autoantibodies (anti-idiotypes), blocks Fc receptors on macrophages, inhibits complement, modulates cytokines, expands regulatory T cells

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Kawasaki disease (with aspirin — prevents coronary aneurysms)
- Dermatomyositis (refractory; approved in USA), pemphigus vulgaris/foliaceus (refractory — 3rd line in the Derma Desk ladder), bullous pemphigoid, mucous membrane pemphigoid, EBA
- SJS/TEN (controversial benefit), scleromyxoedema (first line), pyoderma gangrenosum, chronic urticaria (refractory), vasculitis, primary immunodeficiency, ITP

## Dose & formulations
- Immunomodulatory dose: 2 g/kg per cycle divided over 2–5 days, repeated every 4 weeks
- TEN: 1 g/kg/day for 3 days (total 3 g/kg) in studies
- Infuse slowly (start 0.5 mL/kg/h and increase)

## Adverse effects
- Infusion reactions (headache, chills, flushing, back pain) — slow rate, premedicate
- Aseptic meningitis, thrombosis (stroke, MI — hyperviscosity), acute kidney injury (sucrose-containing products), haemolysis (anti-A/B antibodies)
- Anaphylaxis in IgA-deficient patients with anti-IgA antibodies
- Eczematous/pompholyx-like eruptions after infusion

## Contraindications
- IgA deficiency with anti-IgA antibodies (use IgA-depleted product); caution in renal failure, thrombosis risk, heart failure

## Drug interactions
- Live vaccines: response reduced (delay for months)

## Monitoring
- Baseline IgA level, renal function, CBC; BP and vitals during infusion; hydration

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe in pregnancy.

## Viva points
- FcRn saturation increases IgG catabolism
- Check IgA levels before first infusion
- 2 g/kg per cycle for autoimmune disease
- Scleromyxoedema — IVIG is first-line

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.36 (Intravenous immunoglobulin); Khopkar (Intravenous immunoglobulins). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
